        The Cathedral of Our Lady of Walsingham, established in 1984 under the Pastoral Provision of Pope John Paul II, was the first Catholic parish in the United States to be dedicated to Our Lady under this title. Our Lady of Walsingham was named Principal Church of the Personal Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter on January 1, 2012 and was elevated to a cathedral after the appointment of the Ordinariate's first bishop, the Most Rev. Steven J. Lopes. All are welcome to worship with us, as well as to visit the outdoor Shrine of Our Lady of Walsingham .

        Adult Forum: Sundays 9:45-10:45

         ♰ Et Verbum Caro Factum Est ♰ And The Word Was Made Flesh ♰
         
        Incarnation Catholic Church was founded initially as the Church of the Incarnation, an Anglican ecclesial body, in the early 1980’s.  The congregation was established as a parish of the Traditional Anglican Communion, a body that as part of its by-laws sought to restore union with the Roman Catholic Church.  In 2012, the parish was formally received into full communion through the Personal Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter. 
         
        Incarnation is now home to over 400 parishioners, and we live by the principles of faith, tradition and reverence.  
         
        “If one is asked, what is the mission of the Ordinariate of the Chair of St. Peter? The answer to that question need not take a lot to memorize and present. The answer is evangelism.”
        – Rev. William Holiday
         
        For more information contact Fr. William P. Holiday, Parochial Administrator, or visit us at https://www.incarnationcc.org

        We are a community of Catholics, most of us former Anglicans, located in Victoria, BC Canada who sought unity with the Catholic Church under the terms of Pope Benedict XVI's Apostolic Constitution,  Anglicanorum coetibus.  Our original members were received into the Catholic Church at St. Andrew's Cathedral in Victoria on Sunday the 15th of April, 2012. Since that time, other former Anglicans and Roman Catholics have joined us. We are part of the Ordinariate's Canadian Deanery of St John the Baptist.

        St. John the Baptist Catholic Church is a Catholic parish in the missionary Diocese of the Personal Ordinariate of the Chair of Saint Peter. We are located in Bridgeport, PA and serve the Philadelphia area.  We celebrate the sacred liturgy of the Catholic Church with an “Anglican inflection.” However, we do not exist just for Anglicans who wish to become Catholic. Our mission encompasses any and all who desire full communion with the Catholic Church. As “any Catholic may worship in any Catholic parish,” our doors are open to any and all within the Catholic Church, as well as visitors who are curious about the Catholic faith and the beauty of our liturgy.

        St John’s is a friendly, family-oriented and welcoming Ordinariate parish, worshipping in one of Calgary’s oldest churches, located in historic Inglewood, the oldest neighbourhood in the city. The former Anglican parish was founded in 1905 (as part of the Church of England in Canada), and the present church dates from 1911, a living tribute to the work and ministry of the parish’s second rector, Canon Gervase Edward Gale. It was designated as a Municipal Historic Resource in 2010.  Rooted in Catholic teaching and practice our worship is infused with our noble Anglican liturgical, musical and spiritual patrimony, as reflected in our liturgy, preaching and teaching.   We are a growing parish, celebrating the joy of being Catholic, striving to make disciples of all nations, and conscious of our call to help heal the divisions in Christendom.  We rejoice in the historic gesture of Pope Benedict XVI in giving us the opportunity to enter the fullness of Catholic life in communion with the Apostolic See whilst retaining elements of the patrimony of our Anglican tradition as a precious gift “ nourishing the faith of the mem bers of the Ordinariate and as a treasure to be shared .”

        St. Thomas More is a friendly, growing, and thriving Catholic congregation in Scranton, Pennsylvania with a mission to welcome people of all walks of life to the Catholic Church through beautiful worship, authentic fellowship, robust teaching, compassionate outreach, and joy in sharing the Good News. Our founding members and our priest were members of a local Episcopal parish who came into the Catholic Church as an intact congregation in 2005, but our membership has expanded in both its numbers and its diversity ever since, as we have welcomed people of many other backgrounds into our fellowship: Lifelong Catholics, lapsed Catholics rediscovering the Church, Protestants exploring the Catholic faith, and pre-Christian seekers wanting to learn more about Jesus.

        Below you can take a virtual tour of St. Thomas More Church and parish hall. You will also note a small chevron-shaped arrows on the floor; clicking these will take you further along the tour in the direction they point, including the High Altar, narthex, front porch, etc.

        To view the parish hall, follow the floor of the narthex or front porch, where you will see a floor arrow pointing sideways rather than up and down the center axis. Clicking that arrow will take you downstairs to the Parish Hall, where you can manipulate the panoramic view as described above.
